## Summary

The audit runner's code-quality scan is documented to lint only the work item's changed files (`SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1: "the code-quality scan runs only over the git changed-file list … not the full repo"), but it silently falls back to a **whole-repo** scan whenever the changed-file list is empty. For an item whose work is already committed to `dev` (the normal post-merge state, and the state the merge gate integrates to), `git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` are both empty, so `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` receives `None` and lints the entire repository. Any pre-existing critical/high ruff finding in an unrelated file then blocks Phase 1 of every audit in that repo — a recurrence of the defect class fixed by `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` ("EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files") and a contradiction of `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1.

## Repro

1. Work item `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm) is merged to `origin/dev`; the local checkout is clean at the delivered commit `66ddbe93`.
2. `git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty.
3. Run `audit_runner.py issue LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS --force`: `_git_changed_files` returns `[]`, so `run_code_quality(files=None)` scans the whole repo.
4. The whole-repo scan returns 4 findings, all outside the item's change set:
   - `ruff F841` (critical) `proxy/tests/test_watchdog_upstream_cancellation.py:197,277`
   - `ruff I001` (medium) `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py:594`, `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503`
5. Phase 1 blocks on the critical findings; every AC is demoted `met → partial` and Phase 2 is skipped; `Ready to close: No`.

Verified directly: `run_code_quality(project_root=<llm>, files=[the item's 4 changed files])` returns **0 findings** — the item's own work is lint-clean.

## Impact (observed)

- The audit of `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (2026-09-26) produced a spurious `Ready to close: No` from findings belonging to other work items. The item was only accepted because the Phase 1 false-positive screen *also* degraded (provider error / concurrency limit), leaving the run fallback-tainted and the lifecycle restored to `completed`/`in_review`.
- Had the screen succeeded, the `F841` findings would have been classified `genuine` and the unrelated item would have been **demoted** `in_review → open`.
- The findings already have tracking items (quality epics): `LP-0MUHSWSI8004AFU4`, `LP-0MUHSWS8M001QY46`, `LP-0MUHVMLGB0056C0K`.

## Suggested fix

- When the git changed-file list is empty, scope the code-quality scan to the item's **Key Files** and/or its committed diff (the commits the merge gate resolved, e.g. `git diff-tree -r --name-only <commit>^..<commit>`), instead of falling back to the whole repo.
- An empty effective scope should lint nothing (skip with a documented reason), never the entire repository.
- Cover the already-merged / clean-checkout case in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For an item whose work is already committed and whose checkout is clean, the audit code-quality scan lints only the item's files (Key Files and/or its delivered commits), never the whole repo.
2. An empty effective scope lints nothing (documented skip), rather than scanning the whole repository.
3. Unit tests cover the empty-changed-file case and assert `run_code_quality` is not invoked with `files=None` (whole repo) for an already-merged item.
4. Re-auditing an item in a repo containing unrelated critical ruff findings no longer reports those findings against that item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` — EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files (completed) — same defect class.
- `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` — Audit: scope code-quality scan to changed files, read-only (completed) — introduced the scoping this bug regresses in the empty-diff case.
- Discovered during the audit of `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9** – Review find related skill (completed)
- **SA-0MLR3JM2I03XOKHC** – TUI update dialog does not create comments when comment box has content (completed)
- **SA-0MM8W6OK5061NLKG** – Audit test suite refactoring (open)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mskb6vwu000rt58, ac1, acceptance, accepted, already (+143 more)

# Repair wl sync for the operator's GitHub-identity checkout

`discovered-from:SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` (created during that item's session; actioned by operator directive).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` in this checkout cannot merge incoming worklog data: the author-identity
gate (SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) refuses all remote `refs/worklog/data` commits because
they are authored by `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` (the operator's
GitHub identity) while the local checkout's `user.email` is `pi@local`. Additional
blockers are 31 incident-era commits from the leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident
(2026-09-26) authored as `t@t.com` — a hardcoded `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` sentinel
that must NOT be whitelisted.

## Existing state

- `.worklog/config.yaml` previously had no `syncAllowedAuthors` — the gate had
  only the strict user.email comparison.
- `refs/worklog/data` history contains 31 contiguous `t@t.com` commits
  (positions `345ea154a..fbf0b5bda`, 2026-09-26) that the gate must keep refusing.
- `wl sync` therefore could not merge or push (`1559 incoming commit(s) fail the
  author-identity gate`; after whitelisting the operator identity: `31`).

## Desired change

1. Add the operator's GitHub noreply email to `syncAllowedAuthors` in
   `.worklog/config.yaml` so legitimate operator-identity commits pass the gate.
2. Purge the 31 incident-era `t@t.com` commits from `refs/worklog/data` history
   (re-parent past the block without changing any tree content), so the gate has
   nothing to refuse.
3. `wl sync` completes and pushes the current SQLite store (incl. SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `wl sync --dry-run` no longer refuses on author identity.
2. **AC2:** `wl sync` completes successfully (merge + push), and
   `SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` appears in `refs/worklog/data`.
3. **AC3:** No `t@t.com`-authored commits remain on `refs/worklog/data`.
4. **AC4:** `t@t.com` is NOT added to `syncAllowedAuthors` (sentinel emails stay
   refused — the quarantine is preserved).
5. **AC5:** The final `refs/worklog/data` tree is identical to the pre-purge tree
   (verified via `git diff`, plus work item count preserved).

## Key Files

- `.worklog/config.yaml` — `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list entry.
- `refs/worklog/data` — incident-block purge (git history rewrite).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: force-push history rewrite on a shared branch.** Mitigation: the rewrite
  only re-parents the post-block linear history; trees are untouched; the loss of
  31 incident-era commits is the intended quarantine. Any clone that fast-forwards
  is unaffected; others receive the rewritten chain on their next fetch.
- **Assumption:** `t@t.com` commits carry no legitimate post-incident data (they
  are in the 2026-09-26 incident window, superseded by the 2026-09-27+
  operator-identity snapshots).

Discovered-from:SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU.

## Summary

`wl sync` refuses to merge inbound worklog commits on refs/worklog/data: 4 commits (66b8e59b, a31dfb9a, 664d5b55, 1afacea2) authored `Sorra the Orc <pi@local>` (2026-10-15) fail the author gate — `pi@local` does not match configured `user.email` (`250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`) and is not in `syncAllowedAuthors`.

This blocks pushing the local close of SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU (and any other local worklog mutations) to origin. Local DB update succeeded; only remote sync is blocked.

## Verified state (2026-10-16 plan session)

- Exactly 4 gating commits, all `pi@local`, after last-synced-ref `9727585074`: `66b8e59b`, `a31dfb9a`, `664d5b55`, `1afacea2` (verified via `git log 97275850..refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`).
- Gate semantics (worklog package `sync.js::checkAuthorIdentity`): a commit passes if author email matches `user.email` OR is in `syncAllowedAuthors`. Empty-email gate is never bypassed.
- 3 older `pi@local` commits (2026-09-16) predate last-synced-ref and are not gating.
- Main-checkout identity is healthy (`check_git_identity.py` → ok); the offending pushes came from a pi session with unset/incorrect identity.
- Stranded data is real: e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC (the earlier config fix) is absent from the local store.

## Decisions (operator, 2026-10-16)

- **Remediation of the 4 stranded commits:** one-time operator-authorized `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` (option a) — the designed escape hatch; no shared-history rewrite; the subsequent correctly-authored push advances last-synced-ref past the offenders.
- **Recurrence prevention:** add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` for this project (operator-chosen option c), so pi-session-authored sync commits pass the gate. This deliberately widens the project gate to accept `pi@local` (empty-email gate still enforced); the general guard `scripts/check_git_identity.py` must NOT be hardened to flag `pi@local` (that would contradict the allow-list).

## Goal

Restore `wl sync` so local worklog mutations push to origin, and prevent recurrence of author-identity refusals for pi-session commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `wl sync` completes without an author-identity refusal, and previously-stranded items (e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC) are present in the local store; `last-synced-ref` advances past the 4 offending commits.
- [ ] **AC2** The one-time `--allow-foreign-author` remediation is operator-authorized and recorded in a comment with the exact command and output (safety-gate provenance).
- [ ] **AC3** `pi@local` is added to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), and a regression test pins that the config allow-list accepts a `pi@local`-authored commit while an arbitrary foreign email is still refused.
- [ ] **AC4** Full test suite passes on a clean build; all changes committed with work-item association.

## Plan (approved 2026-10-16; 3 children, test-first)

1. **Author-gate incident regression tests** (test-first) — drive the gate/guard decision for the `pi@local` allow-list change; red before, green after.
2. **Recover stranded worklog data** (operator-authorized) — one-time `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`, verify stranded items present, last-synced-ref advances.
3. **Add `pi@local` to syncAllowedAuthors** (project allow-list) — `.worklog/config.yaml` change + docs note, depends on 1.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which remediation for the 4 stranded commits — (a) one-time authorized `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`, (b) rewrite the 4 authors and force-update refs/worklog/data, or (c) add `pi@local` to syncAllowedAuthors?" — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): "(a)". Final: one-time authorized `--allow-foreign-author` merge; no history rewrite. Rationale: designed escape hatch, no shared-ref rewrite.
- Q: "Scope of recurrence prevention — (i) harden `check_git_identity.py` to flag `pi@local` + document, (ii) additionally enforce identity at pi-session/worktree setup, (iii) defer?" — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): "Add pi@local to the allow list for this project". Final: option (c) from the remediation list — add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml`; do NOT harden the guard. Note: this intentionally widens the gate for this project (empty-email gate still never bypassed).

## Goal

Route every real-git invocation in the `implement.py` test fixtures through
`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` so a leaked repository-overriding environment
cannot redirect the fixture away from its `tmp_path` sandbox.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixtures in `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_submodules.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_code_freeze_gate.py` use `gs.init_repo`,
  `gs.commit_all`, `gs.add_worktree` and `gs.run_git`; no bare
  `subprocess.run(["git", …])` remains in these files.
- [ ] Each migrated fixture helper has a behavioural regression test proving a
  leaked `GIT_DIR` cannot redirect it (victim repo unchanged; the fixture repo
  resolves under `tmp_path`), mirroring
  `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py::TestEnvironmentIsolation` and
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py::TestRepoHelpersAreHermetic`.
- [ ] Every `implement.py` subprocess runner in these files passes
  `gs.sanitized_git_env()` so a leaked override cannot reach the child's git
  invocations (as already done in
  `tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py::_run_violation_check`).
- [ ] `default_branch` is set correctly so fixtures that relied on a `dev`
  branch (e.g. `git branch dev` after init) do not create a spurious or
  duplicate branch.
- [ ] Fixture identity is injected via the sandbox (`-c user.name=… -c user.email=…`) rather than relying on a repo-local `git config` in the helper; any remaining identity `config` in a migrated helper is explicit and deliberate.
- [ ] All existing behavioural assertions in the five files pass unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace each fixture's `git init` + `config user.*` + `add` + `commit` +
  `branch dev` sequence with `gs.init_repo(..., default_branch="dev")` +
  `gs.commit_all(...)`; replace `git worktree add` with `gs.add_worktree(...)`.
- Keep subprocess-runner helper scripts, but spawn them with
  `env=gs.sanitized_git_env()`.
- Add one hermetic regression test per migrated fixture (victim + leaked

- `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`
- `tests/test_implement_submodules.py`
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`

# Intake Brief — Raise TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY 2→3 with mini-F7 validation

## Problem statement

`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 2` (in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) is an
uncalibrated first cut from SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG. Its sibling knob,
`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, was later right-sized empirically (F7 harness:
8 audits drain in 18.7 s at ceiling 3 vs 12.9 s at ceiling 6, batch-attributable
load delta ≤ 1.63, no swap growth — SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE). During peak multi-agent
traffic the test pool therefore queues more than the host requires, so agents
wait on the bounded test slot while CPUs remain idle. Raising the ceiling to 3
is only safe once per-suite worker pools are bounded
(`SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T`), otherwise more concurrent suites means more load, not
less queuing.

## Users

- **Operators / producers** running several agent sessions that finish with a
  test gate at the same time.
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when three agents hit their test gate
    simultaneously, I want the third suite to start rather than wait up to
    `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (600 s), so wall-clock time-to-green drops without
    pushing the host into swap."
- **Agent sessions** (implement/audit/pre-push gates) that currently block on
  the bounded `"test"` semaphore slot.
  - *User story:* "As an agent, I want my test run to start promptly so I can
    complete build → test → commit without a long slot wait."
- **Maintainers** who need the ceiling to be an evidence-backed number rather
  than a guess.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer, I want the default justified by a
    reproducible measurement committed to the repo, matching the audit-knob
    precedent."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Default raised and documented in code.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` is `3` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; module docstring (line ~24), constant comment (line ~139) and `_test_semaphore_max_workers()` docstring (line ~1308) state the value and cite this work item. Precedence (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env > default) and clamping (values < 1 clamp to 1, invalid values warn and fall back) are unchanged.
- **Mini-F7 measurement gates the change.** An F7-style harness (see Key Files) runs **8 actual suite executions** through the real `run_tests.py` slot path (`--no-cache`, so cache hits cannot bypass the semaphore) at ceiling **3** and ceiling **2** on the 16-core host, sampling process counts, 1/5/15-min load and swap every ≤ 0.5 s via `skill/shared/measure_fanout.py`. Pass gate: batch-attributable load delta **< 4**, **no swap growth**, and 8-execution drain time at ceiling 3 **≤ 1.10 ×** the ceiling-2 drain time. Raw results are recorded in the work item (table) and as a committed JSON artifact (`docs/dev/test-ceiling-validation.json`). Reproduction commands: `python3 skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py --ceiling 2 --n 8 --out /tmp/ceiling-2.json` then the same with `--ceiling 3`.
- **Regression tests pass and the default is pinned.** All existing tests in `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` (17 test functions: 12 module-level + 5 class methods — the seed item's "10" is corrected here) pass unchanged, plus new tests: (a) the resolved default equals `3` with the calibration rationale, and (b) a cross-process run with **no** env override never exceeds 3 active slots. `skill/test/tests/test_nested_semaphore_isolation.py` passes unchanged (isolation contract, SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86).
- **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (env table `2`→`3`, the nested-run deadlock example that names "two concurrent full suites … `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`", and a short calibration subsection linking the measurement), `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` (or a new section documenting this run), and any other doc stating the old default.
- **Reproducible harness.** The harness is committed with a CLI (`--ceiling`, `--n`, `--out`), a per-batch isolated `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, and unit tests covering its argument handling and report shape; the documented invocation reproduces the measurement.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new default (build → test → commit order per AGENTS.md).
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **Ordering:** implementation must not merge before `SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T`
  (per-suite vitest/tinypool pools bounded) is complete; the measurement is
  only meaningful afterwards. This item is currently `blocked` on that item.
- **Measure attributable deltas, not absolute load.** The host usually carries
  unrelated agent traffic; the precedent (SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE) uses
  batch-attributable delta because absolute "load < 16" is not observable.
  Sample the baseline immediately before the batch and report both.
- **Do not change semantics:** bounded-wait, jitter (`TEST_LOCK_JITTER`), cache
  behaviour (hits never acquire a slot), the separate `"audit"`/`"audit-host"`
  namespaces, and the nested-run isolation contract stay as-is.
- **Do not relax nested-run isolation.** At default 3 the documented deadlock
  scenario shifts from two to three concurrent full suites; update the prose
  rather than weakening isolation. Replacing opt-in isolation is out of scope
  (SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF).
- **Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`** (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).
- The repo is the canonical source for `skill/`, so editing
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` is explicitly in scope for this item.

## Existing state

| Knob | Default | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | **2** | `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:138-139` | Uncalibrated first cut (SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG) |
| `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 600 s | `run_tests.py:140-141` | Bounded wait for a free slot |
| `TEST_LOCK_JITTER` | 0.1 | `run_tests.py:145-146` | Per-waiter deadline stagger (SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD) |
| `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | 6 | `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` | F7-calibrated precedent |
| F7 harness | — | `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` | Audit-only today: it launches `audit_runner.py issue` with a mock pi |
| Measurement tool | — | `skill/shared/measure_fanout.py` | Read-only process/load/swap sampler |

- The semaphore binds on **actual executions only**; `--summary`/cache hits
  never acquire a slot, so the harness must use `--no-cache` to produce real
  concurrency.
- This repository has **no vitest suites** (pytest + `node --test`); the
  per-suite worker fan-out fixed by the blocker lives in consumer repos
  (e.g. TCE). The harness therefore needs a deterministic synthetic suite
  payload (a `suiteCommands` entry in a throwaway repo that burns a bounded
  number of worker processes for a fixed duration), mirroring F7's mock-pi
  approach so the measurement is quick and non-intrusive.
- Docs stating the old default: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` lines 131,
  215. No literal default appears in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
  or `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Desired change

- Raise the default to 3 and make the rationale (calibration, blocker
  dependency, nested-isolation caveat) explicit at the constant and in the
  docstrings.
- Add a test-suite fan-out harness (F7-style, synthetic payload) that measures
  drain time, load delta and swap delta at ceilings 2 and 3, and commit the
  raw artifact.
- Update the test-skill reference (table, nested-deadlock example, calibration
  subsection) and the F7 validation report.
- Extend the semaphore test suite with the default-pinning and
  default-ceiling cross-process tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Raise `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` to 3;
  update module docstring, constant comment and `_test_semaphore_max_workers()`
  docstring with the calibrated value and citation.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — Add default-pinning test
  (resolved default == 3 with rationale) and a cross-process test proving the
  un-overridden default bounds concurrency to ≤ 3.
- `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` *(or a new sibling
  `skill/shared/validate_test_fanout.py`)* — Add the test-suite ceiling mode:
  throwaway repo + `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`, N concurrent
  `run_tests.py --no-cache` executions, per-batch `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, sampler.
- `tests/test_validate_fanout.py` *(or the new harness's test module)* — Unit
  tests for harness argument handling, ceiling propagation and report shape.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — Env table default, nested-run deadlock
  example, calibration subsection.
- `docs/dev/fanout-validation-report.md` — Measurement method, results table,
  conclusion for the test ceiling.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA` — discovery source (flags the uncalibrated default).
- `SA-0MVE98T1M006A17T` — **blocker**: bound per-suite vitest/tinypool worker

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-subscription on small hosts.** A fixed default of 3 could add
  load on an 8-core host or a repo whose suite spawns many workers. Mitigation:
  the value is only raised after the blocker bounds per-suite pools; repos that
  must never overlap browser stages still set `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`
  (documented escape hatch).
- **Risk: synthetic payload does not represent real suites.** Mitigation:
  document what the harness models (suite-level concurrency through the real
  semaphore path with a bounded worker fan-out) and pair the measurement with
  the blocker's per-suite evidence; do not claim it proves per-suite behaviour.
- **Risk: flaky load measurements on a busy shared host.** Mitigation:
  attributable-delta method, repeated runs, and reporting the baseline; never

# Verify item-data-only audit freshness contract

**Parent:** SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 (Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change)

**User story:** As an audit operator, I want independent, executable proof that a stored audit is invalidated *only* by a change to this work item's own audited data (title/description/ACs/Key Files), so that unrelated repository activity can never silently invalidate or (worse) mask a stale audit.

**Why a separate verification item:** the parent's AC8 requires that no existing coverage is silently dropped. This item owns that guarantee: it enumerates the old per-touched-path / comment-contribution contract, proves each case is now asserted the *new* way, and adds mutation-style guards that fail if any git- or comment-derived component is ever reintroduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Non-invalidation regression tests assert the fingerprint is **unchanged** across all three previously-invalidating conditions: (a) HEAD movement caused by another work item's commit, (b) uncommitted/untracked working-tree changes anywhere in the repo, (c) committed, staged or dirty changes **to a file this item itself touched** (the direct reversal of `test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` / `..._dirty` / `..._staged` and `test_tool_artefact_rewrite_invalidates`).
2. Invalidation regression tests assert the fingerprint **changes** when the item's title changes, when its description/ACs change, and when its `Key Files` section changes.
3. Non-invalidation tests assert the fingerprint is unchanged after: adding a comment (including a comment recording a commit hash), and changing `status` / `stage` / `priority` / `assignee` / `sortIndex` (all of which move `updatedAt`).
4. A mutation-style guard asserts `_compute_content_fingerprint` makes **zero** git calls: with the runner's git-executing helpers patched to raise, a fingerprint is still returned; and an exact-payload test asserts the hashed payload keys are exactly the item-data schema (no `path_states`, no `head`/`worktree`, no comment-derived keys), so reintroducing a component fails a test.
5. Versioned-line tests: the persisted report's `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hex>` line round-trips through `_extract_content_fingerprint`; an unversioned legacy line (`Audit content fingerprint: <hex>`) makes `_extract_content_fingerprint` return `None` and the gate falls back to the time floor (fresh inside `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS` + persist-write tolerance, stale beyond it); `check-freshness --json` reports `hasFingerprint: false` for a legacy v1 report and `true` for a v2 report.
6. Child-reuse coverage: `_get_child_audit_verdict` / `_child_content_changed` reuse a child whose own data is unchanged, and treat a title/description change as stale.
7. A ledger comment on this item lists **every** pre-existing freshness test that was rewritten, kept or removed, with the reason for each — so nothing is silently dropped (parent AC8).
8. `skill/audit/tests` and `skill/ship` unit tests pass via `/skill:test` (changed scope), with the verification evidence (test names + file:line) recorded in a comment.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (`TestContentFreshnessGate` plus a new item-data-only class) and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`.
- Reuse the existing `_FakeGitRepo` / `mock.patch.object` fixtures; add the zero-git-call guard by patching the git-executing helper with a `RuntimeError`-raising stub.
- Record the migrated-test ledger as a `wl comment add` on this item.
- Run the changed-scope suite through `/skill:test`; do not invoke pytest directly.

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production behaviour changes in this item; any gap found is reported on the owning implementation item (SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 children) rather than fixed here out of scope.
- Read-only: no `pi` calls, no full-audit pipeline execution needed.
